meta_description: Voyage ETA on a vessel-performance spine — schedule reliability up 8 points and buffer fuel down 6% without slipping promises

blocks.x: Voyage ETA on a vessel-performance spine — schedule reliability up 8 points and buffer fuel down 6% without slipping promises
Identity withheld — a container line whose schedule was a promise its fleet kept by carrying fuel for the worst case. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.
The baseline quarter weighed the worst case: schedule reliability 64%, 6% of bunker spend covering schedule risk, and customers' planning teams building their own delays around the line's variance.
ETA models used generic vessel curves; actual hull conditions, trim and weather routing lived with captains. The network's planners and the bridge never shared a number.

We built the vessel spine: per-hull performance curves learned from voyage data, weather-routed ETA predictions produced per leg and shared to network planning in one model, slow-steaming opportunities flagged where the schedule allowed, and the customer-facing promise computed from the same spine operations trusts. Captains reviewed the curves; the sea kept its vote.
